title: Cell Membrane and Materials Movement Core Test
description: Core practice for model how cell membranes help cells exchange materials while maintaining workable internal conditions.

questions.prompt: What is one main role of the cell membrane?
questions.questionText: What is one main role of the cell membrane?
options: to help control what moves into and out of a cell
questions.correctAnswer: to help control what moves into and out of a cell
questions.explanation: The membrane is a selective boundary.

questions.prompt: A potato slice loses mass in salty water. Which explanation best fits?
questions.questionText: A potato slice loses mass in salty water. Which explanation best fits?
options: Water moved out of cells because the outside was saltier.
questions.correctAnswer: Water moved out of cells because the outside was saltier.
questions.explanation: The outside condition can drive water movement.

questions.prompt: Which model is strongest?
questions.questionText: Which model is strongest?
options: outside condition -> concentration difference -> membrane movement -> cell effect
cell color -> favorite food -> no data
questions.correctAnswer: outside condition -> concentration difference -> membrane movement -> cell effect
questions.explanation: The chain connects cause and cell effect.

questions.prompt: What does diffusion describe?
questions.questionText: What does diffusion describe?
options: particles spreading from more crowded to less crowded areas
questions.correctAnswer: particles spreading from more crowded to less crowded areas
questions.explanation: Diffusion follows concentration patterns.

questions.prompt: A student says the membrane blocks all materials. What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student says the membrane blocks all materials. What is the best correction?
options: Cells exchange materials through controlled movement across the membrane.
questions.correctAnswer: Cells exchange materials through controlled movement across the membrane.
questions.explanation: Cells must take in and release materials.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports water movement?
questions.questionText: Which evidence best supports water movement?
options: one slice has a longer name
same-size cucumber slices have different mass after salt and plain-water treatments
questions.correctAnswer: same-size cucumber slices have different mass after salt and plain-water treatments
questions.explanation: A controlled before-and-after comparison is evidence.

questions.prompt: Why should the cucumber slices be the same size?
questions.questionText: Why should the cucumber slices be the same size?
options: to control variables so the water movement comparison is fair
questions.correctAnswer: to control variables so the water movement comparison is fair
questions.explanation: Fair tests change one main variable.

questions.prompt: A cell placed in plain water swells. What likely moved?
questions.questionText: A cell placed in plain water swells. What likely moved?
questions.correctAnswer: water moved into the cell
questions.explanation: Water movement can change cell size.

questions.prompt: Which question tests understanding?
questions.questionText: Which question tests understanding?
options: How would the result change if the outside solution were less salty?
How long is the word membrane?
questions.correctAnswer: How would the result change if the outside solution were less salty?
questions.explanation: Changing the condition tests the model.

questions.prompt: A dye drop spreads through still water. What concept does this model?
questions.questionText: A dye drop spreads through still water. What concept does this model?
questions.correctAnswer: diffusion
questions.explanation: The dye spreads from high to low concentration.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern supports diffusion?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern supports diffusion?
options: color is darkest near the drop at first, then spreads outward over time
color stays only in the label
questions.correctAnswer: color is darkest near the drop at first, then spreads outward over time
questions.explanation: Spreading over time is a diffusion pattern.

questions.prompt: Why do cells need oxygen to move in?
questions.questionText: Why do cells need oxygen to move in?
options: oxygen is used by cells during cellular respiration
questions.correctAnswer: oxygen is used by cells during cellular respiration
questions.explanation: Cells need materials for processes.

questions.prompt: Which claim overreaches?
questions.questionText: Which claim overreaches?
options: This one cucumber test proves every membrane moves every material the same way.
The salty condition may cause water loss.
More trials would strengthen the claim.
questions.correctAnswer: This one cucumber test proves every membrane moves every material the same way.
questions.explanation: One test should not be overgeneralized.

questions.prompt: A membrane lets water through more easily than large starch molecules. What does selective mean?
questions.questionText: A membrane lets water through more easily than large starch molecules. What does selective mean?
options: some materials cross more easily than others
questions.correctAnswer: some materials cross more easily than others
questions.explanation: Selective boundaries do not treat all materials the same.

questions.prompt: What should a graph of potato mass in salty water show if water leaves cells?
questions.questionText: What should a graph of potato mass in salty water show if water leaves cells?
options: mass increases because labels are bigger
questions.correctAnswer: mass decreases over time
questions.explanation: Water loss can reduce mass.

questions.prompt: A freshwater organism is moved to very salty water and cells lose water. What might happen?
questions.questionText: A freshwater organism is moved to very salty water and cells lose water. What might happen?
options: cell processes may be stressed because internal conditions change
questions.correctAnswer: cell processes may be stressed because internal conditions change
questions.explanation: Water balance matters for cell function.

questions.prompt: Which result would weaken the salt-water claim?
questions.questionText: Which result would weaken the salt-water claim?
options: all slices changed the same way, including the no-salt control
repeated trials showed similar water loss
the salty slice became more flexible
questions.correctAnswer: all slices changed the same way, including the no-salt control
questions.explanation: If the control changes the same way, salt may not be the cause.

questions.prompt: Why connect membrane movement to homeostasis?
questions.questionText: Why connect membrane movement to homeostasis?
options: controlled exchange helps cells keep workable internal conditions
questions.correctAnswer: controlled exchange helps cells keep workable internal conditions
questions.explanation: Material movement supports internal balance.

questions.prompt: Which explanation is most scientific?
questions.questionText: Which explanation is most scientific?
options: The plate pulled out the water with feelings.
The salt outside created a concentration difference that led to water movement out of cells.
questions.correctAnswer: The salt outside created a concentration difference that led to water movement out of cells.
questions.explanation: Scientific explanations use mechanisms.

questions.prompt: A student changes both salt amount and slice thickness. What problem does this create?
questions.questionText: A student changes both salt amount and slice thickness. What problem does this create?
options: It is harder to know which variable caused the result.
It makes the result automatically perfect.
It removes all need for data.
questions.correctAnswer: It is harder to know which variable caused the result.
questions.explanation: Multiple changed variables weaken claims.

questions.prompt: Which evidence combines model and data?
questions.questionText: Which evidence combines model and data?
options: a diagram of water leaving cells plus measured mass loss
a sketch with no labels and no measurements
questions.correctAnswer: a diagram of water leaving cells plus measured mass loss
questions.explanation: Models and measurements support each other.

questions.prompt: If oxygen is higher outside a cell than inside, which movement is likely?
questions.questionText: If oxygen is higher outside a cell than inside, which movement is likely?
options: oxygen tends to diffuse into the cell
questions.correctAnswer: oxygen tends to diffuse into the cell
questions.explanation: Diffusion tends from high to low concentration.

questions.prompt: Why is the membrane not the same as a wall around a room?
questions.questionText: Why is the membrane not the same as a wall around a room?
options: it has no relationship to cells
it is made of desk wood
it is a living boundary involved in selective material exchange
questions.correctAnswer: it is a living boundary involved in selective material exchange
questions.explanation: The analogy has limits.

questions.prompt: Which final summary is best?
questions.questionText: Which final summary is best?
options: Cell membranes help manage material movement, and concentration differences can affect cell conditions.
Particles move because they choose goals.
questions.correctAnswer: Cell membranes help manage material movement, and concentration differences can affect cell conditions.
questions.explanation: This captures boundary, movement, and effect.

questions.prompt: What would be the best next investigation?
questions.questionText: What would be the best next investigation?
options: compare several salt concentrations while keeping sample size and time constant
questions.correctAnswer: compare several salt concentrations while keeping sample size and time constant
questions.explanation: A range of concentrations tests the model.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best avoids memorizing only vocabulary?
questions.questionText: Which explanation best avoids memorizing only vocabulary?
options: It repeats the bold word only.
It connects the model, evidence, and cause/effect relationship.
questions.correctAnswer: It connects the model, evidence, and cause/effect relationship.
questions.explanation: Understanding means using the idea.

questions.prompt: Which type of evidence would make the claim stronger?
questions.questionText: Which type of evidence would make the claim stronger?
questions.correctAnswer: repeated observations under controlled conditions
questions.explanation: Repeated controlled observations strengthen claims.

questions.prompt: What should a careful scientist avoid?
questions.questionText: What should a careful scientist avoid?
options: changing several variables and then claiming one cause with certainty
questions.correctAnswer: changing several variables and then claiming one cause with certainty
questions.explanation: Fair tests protect conclusions.

questions.prompt: Which prompt asks for transfer?
questions.questionText: Which prompt asks for transfer?
options: How would the model apply if the organism, material, or ecosystem changed?
What is the first letter of the topic?
questions.correctAnswer: How would the model apply if the organism, material, or ecosystem changed?
questions.explanation: Transfer means applying the idea to new details.

questions.prompt: Which final habit helps in science?
questions.questionText: Which final habit helps in science?
options: explain the evidence before choosing the claim
questions.correctAnswer: explain the evidence before choosing the claim
questions.explanation: Claims should follow evidence.
